### Thread 1 — `js/configLoader.js` line 458

**dmtools-factory-bot** (2026-10-18):
🚨 **BLOCKING: dynamic `customParams[key]` access breaks `agentDocGenerator` static analysis → red `docs-freshness` CI**

This line is why the `docs-freshness` check is red on this head. The doc generator (`js/agentDocGenerator.js:268-269`) discovers supported `customParams` keys from JS sources with two regexes:

```javascript
/customParams\.([a-zA_$][\w$]*(?:\.[a-zA_$][\w$]*)*)/g,
/customParams\[['"]([\w.]+)['"]\]/g
```

Both only match **literal** property access. Before this PR, `configLoader.js` contained `customParams.branchNamingFnPath` and `customParams.prSearchFnPath` as static reads, so every generated agent doc listed those two keys. After the refactor, the only read is `customParams[key]` with a variable key — neither regex matches, so the keys silently vanish from the analysis.

Verified locally:
- On `origin/main`: `node js/agentDocGenerator.js` → zero diff.
- On this branch: same command → 49 generated files changed (296 deletions), all of them removing `branchNamingFnPath` / `prSearchFnPath` from the documented customParams.
- The workflow then fails at `git diff --exit-code -- docs/agents/generated` — exactly the red `docs-freshness` check in `ci_failures.md`.

Note that simply committing the regenerated docs is **not** a valid fix: those keys are still fully supported hooks (the code loads them at `js/configLoader.js:534-535`), so the regenerated docs would be wrong — they'd stop documenting live features.

**Suggested fix** — keep the two keys statically visible to the generator, e.g. read them via literal member access at the call sites:

```javascript
// instead of the generic key argument:
function loadCustomParamFnHook(target, path, exportKey) { ... }
loadCustomParamFnHook(config.git, customParams.branchNamingFnPath, 'branchNamingFn');
loadCustomParamFnHook(config, customParams.prSearchFnPath, 'prSearchFn');
```

or add a `// customParams.branchNamingFnPath / customParams.prSearchFnPath` marker comment if you prefer to keep the current helper shape (regexes also match comments' text only when written as real member access — a plain comment with `customParams.branchNamingFnPath` in it does match the first regex, but the explicit-argument form above is less fragile). # PR Discussion History

_Previous review discussions for PR #1056._

> ℹ️ **1 machine notice(s) excluded (arming/status boilerplate — never reply targets).**

## Review Threads (Inline Comments)

### Thread 1 — `js/configLoader.js` line 458

**dmtools-factory-bot** (2026-10-18):
🚨 **BLOCKING: dynamic `customParams[key]` access breaks `agentDocGenerator` static analysis → red `docs-freshness` CI**

This line is why the `docs-freshness` check is red on this head. The doc generator (`js/agentDocGenerator.js:268-269`) discovers supported `customParams` keys from JS sources with two regexes:

```javascript
/customParams\.([a-zA_$][\w$]*(?:\.[a-zA_$][\w$]*)*)/g,
/customParams\[['"]([\w.]+)['"]\]/g
```

Both only match **literal** property access. Before this PR, `configLoader.js` contained `customParams.branchNamingFnPath` and `customParams.prSearchFnPath` as static reads, so every generated agent doc listed those two keys. After the refactor, the only read is `customParams[key]` with a variable key — neither regex matches, so the keys silently vanish from the analysis.

Verified locally:
- On `origin/main`: `node js/agentDocGenerator.js` → zero diff.
- On this branch: same command → 49 generated files changed (296 deletions), all of them removing `branchNamingFnPath` / `prSearchFnPath` from the documented customParams.
- The workflow then fails at `git diff --exit-code -- docs/agents/generated` — exactly the red `docs-freshness` check in `ci_failures.md`.

Note that simply committing the regenerated docs is **not** a valid fix: those keys are still fully supported hooks (the code loads them at `js/configLoader.js:534-535`), so the regenerated docs would be wrong — they'd stop documenting live features.

**Suggested fix** — keep the two keys statically visible to the generator, e.g. read them via literal member access at the call sites:

```javascript
// instead of the generic key argument:

# PR Discussion History

## Review Threads (Inline Comments)

### Thread 1 — `js/configLoader.js` line 458

**dmtools-factory-bot** (2026-10-18):
🚨 **BLOCKING: dynamic `customParams[key]` access breaks `agentDocGenerator` static analysis → red `docs-freshness` CI**

This line is why the `docs-freshness` check is red on this head. The doc generator (`js/agentDocGenerator.js:268-269`) discovers supported `customParams` keys from JS sources with two regexes:

```javascript
/customParams\.([a-zA_$][\w$]*(?:\.[a-zA_$][\w$]*)*)/g,
/customParams\[['"]([\w.]+)['"]\]/g
```

Both only match **literal** property access. Before this PR, `configLoader.js` contained `customParams.branchNamingFnPath` and `customParams.prSearchFnPath` as static reads, so every generated agent doc listed those two keys. After the refactor, the only read is `customParams[key]` with a variable key — neither regex matches, so the keys silently vanish from the analysis.

Verified locally:
- On `origin/main`: `node js/agentDocGenerator.js` → zero diff.
- On this branch: same command → 49 generated files changed (296 deletions), all of them removing `branchNamingFnPath` / `prSearchFnPath` from the documented customParams.
- The workflow then fails at `git diff --exit-code -- docs/agents/generated` — exactly the red `docs-freshness` check in `ci_failures.md`.

Note that simply committing the regenerated docs is **not** a valid fix: those keys are still fully supported hooks (the code loads them at `js/configLoader.js:534-535`), so the regenerated docs would be wrong — they'd stop documenting live features.

**Suggested fix** — keep the two keys statically visible to the generator, e.g. read them via literal member access at the call sites:

```javascript
// instead of the generic key argument:
function loadCustomParamFnHook(target, path, exportKey) { ... }
loadCustomParamFnHook(config.git, customParams.branchNamingFnPath, 'branchNamingFn');
loadCustomParamFnHook(config, customParams.prSearchFnPath, 'prSearchFn');
```

or add a `// customParams.branchNamingFnPath / customParams.prSearchFnPath` marker comment if you prefer to keep the current helper shape (regexes also match comments' text only when written as real member access — a plain comment with `customParams.branchNamingFnPath` in it does match the first regex, but the explicit-argument form above is less fragile). Then re-run `node js/agentDocGenerator.js` and confirm `git diff --exit-code -- docs/agents/generated` is clean.

# gh-1039: [CRAP] configLoader.loadProjectConfig (54) + common/buildEncodedConfig.buildEncodedConfig (57)

## Description

## Problem
`js/configLoader.js::loadProjectConfig` **54.2** and `js/common/buildEncodedConfig.js::buildEncodedConfig` **57**: every agent loads project config through these. Source precedence (configPath, customParams, agentConfigsDir, defaults) must not change.

## Goal
Bring each named function under CRAP 30 by extracting pure parse/build/decide helpers and covering every branch with characterization tests. Same tracker/SCM/git/file calls in the same order.

## Acceptance
- Behaviour unchanged; each named function at or below the target; no regression; CI `crap` check green and the node harness stays green (canonical runner: `dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_all.json`).
- No code path removed; uncovered paths get a characterization test.

## Rules (read before starting)
- **Pure refactor, behaviour-preserving, backward compatible.** Same exports, same signatures, same return shapes, same log lines/side effects, same tracker/SCM calls in the same order. No config or API changes.
- **Tests first:** add characterization tests that pin the current behaviour of the paths you touch (the node harness: `dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_all.json`), then extract pure helpers (`parse*`/`build*`/`decide*`) from the big function and test those directly. Raising coverage on the function counts as much as splitting it.
- **CRAP gate:** Quality/`crap` compares this PR with the released baseline (`crap-baseline` release). The target function must go DOWN, no function may go up, new functions must be <= 8 (CRAP = CC² + CC at 0% coverage, so an untested helper needs CC <= 2 — or cover it). `crap:improved` is set automatically when it dropped. The baseline is updated by CI after the merge — do **not** commit a baseline file.
- Measure locally: `node ci/run_with_coverage.js …` then `crap4js . --coverage … --threshold 8 --baseline <released crap-baseline.json>` (see .github/workflows/quality.yml).
- Do not "fix" CRAP by deleting tests, adding `/* istanbul ignore */`, or excluding files.

### Thread 1 — `js/configLoader.js` line 458

**dmtools-factory-bot** (2026-10-18):
🚨 **BLOCKING: dynamic `customParams[key]` access breaks `agentDocGenerator` static analysis → red `docs-freshness` CI**

This line is why the `docs-freshness` check is red on this head. The doc generator (`js/agentDocGenerator.js:268-269`) discovers supported `customParams` keys from JS sources with two regexes:

```javascript
/customParams\.([a-zA_$][\w$]*(?:\.[a-zA_$][\w$]*)*)/g,
/customParams\[['"]([\w.]+)['"]\]/g
```

Both only match **literal** property access. Before this PR, `configLoader.js` contained `customParams.branchNamingFnPath` and `customParams.prSearchFnPath` as static reads, so every generated agent doc listed those two keys. After the refactor, the only read is `customParams[key]` with a variable key — neither regex matches, so the keys silently vanish from the analysis.

Verified locally:
- On `origin/main`: `node js/agentDocGenerator.js` → zero diff.
- On this branch: same command → 49 generated files changed (296 deletions), all of them removing `branchNamingFnPath` / `prSearchFnPath` from the documented customParams.
- The workflow then fails at `git diff --exit-code -- docs/agents/generated` — exactly the red `docs-freshness` check in `ci_failures.md`.

Note that simply committing the regenerated docs is **not** a valid fix: those keys are still fully supported hooks (the code loads them at `js/configLoader.js:534-535`), so the regenerated docs would be wrong — they'd stop documenting live features.

**Suggested fix** — keep the two keys statically visible to the generator, e.g. read them via literal member access at the call sites:

```javascript
// instead of the generic key argument:
function loadCustomParamFnHook(target, path, exportKey) { ... }
loadCustomParamFnHook(config.git, customParams.branchNamingFnPath, 'branchNamingFn');
loadCustomParamFnHook(config, customParams.prSearchFnPath, 'prSearchFn');
```

or add a `// customParams.branchNamingFnPath / customParams.prSearchFnPath` marker comment if you prefer to keep the current helper shape (regexes also match comments' text only when written as real member access — a plain comment with `customParams.branchNamingFnPath` in it does match the first regex, but the explicit-argument form above is less fragile). # gh-1039: [CRAP] configLoader.loadProjectConfig (54) + common/buildEncodedConfig.buildEncodedConfig (57)

## Description

## Problem
`js/configLoader.js::loadProjectConfig` **54.2** and `js/common/buildEncodedConfig.js::buildEncodedConfig` **57**: every agent loads project config through these. Source precedence (configPath, customParams, agentConfigsDir, defaults) must not change.

## Goal
Bring each named function under CRAP 30 by extracting pure parse/build/decide helpers and covering every branch with characterization tests. Same tracker/SCM/git/file calls in the same order.

## Acceptance
- Behaviour unchanged; each named function at or below the target; no regression; CI `crap` check green and the node harness stays green (canonical runner: `dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_all.json`).
- No code path removed; uncovered paths get a characterization test.

## Rules (read before starting)
- **Pure refactor, behaviour-preserving, backward compatible.** Same exports, same signatures, same return shapes, same log lines/side effects, same tracker/SCM calls in the same order. No config or API changes.
- **Tests first:** add characterization tests that pin the current behaviour of the paths you touch (the node harness: `dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_all.json`), then extract pure helpers (`parse*`/`build*`/`decide*`) from the big function and test those directly. Raising coverage on the function counts as much as splitting it.
- **CRAP gate:** Quality/`crap` compares this PR with the released baseline (`crap-baseline` release). The target function must go DOWN, no function may go up, new functions must be <= 8 (CRAP = CC² + CC at 0% coverage, so an untested helper needs CC <= 2 — or cover it). `crap:improved` is set automatically when it dropped. The baseline is updated by CI after the merge — do **not** commit a baseline file.
- Measure locally: `node ci/run_with_coverage.js …` then `crap4js . --coverage … --threshold 8 --baseline <released crap-baseline.json>` (see .github/workflows/quality.yml).
- Do not "fix" CRAP by deleting tests, adding `/* istanbul ignore */`, or excluding files.

## Review Threads (Inline Comments)

### Thread 1 — `js/configLoader.js` line 458

**dmtools-factory-bot** (2026-10-18):
🚨 **BLOCKING: dynamic `customParams[key]` access breaks `agentDocGenerator` static analysis → red `docs-freshness` CI**

This line is why the `docs-freshness` check is red on this head. The doc generator (`js/agentDocGenerator.js:268-269`) discovers supported `customParams` keys from JS sources with two regexes:

```javascript
/customParams\.([a-zA_$][\w$]*(?:\.[a-zA_$][\w$]*)*)/g,
/customParams\[['"]([\w.]+)['"]\]/g
```

Both only match **literal** property access. Before this PR, `configLoader.js` contained `customParams.branchNamingFnPath` and `customParams.prSearchFnPath` as static reads, so every generated agent doc listed those two keys. After the refactor, the only read is `customParams[key]` with a variable key — neither regex matches, so the keys silently vanish from the analysis.

Verified locally:
- On `origin/main`: `node js/agentDocGenerator.js` → zero diff.
- On this branch: same command → 49 generated files changed (296 deletions), all of them removing `branchNamingFnPath` / `prSearchFnPath` from the documented customParams.
- The workflow then fails at `git diff --exit-code -- docs/agents/generated` — exactly the red `docs-freshness` check in `ci_failures.md`.

Note that simply committing the regenerated docs is **not** a valid fix: those keys are still fully supported hooks (the code loads them at `js/configLoader.js:534-535`), so the regenerated docs would be wrong — they'd stop documenting live features.

**Suggested fix** — keep the two keys statically visible to the generator, e.g. read them via literal member access at the call sites:

```javascript
// instead of the generic key argument:
function loadCustomParamFnHook(target, path, exportKey) { ... }
loadCustomParamFnHook(config.git, customParams.branchNamingFnPath, 'branchNamingFn');
loadCustomParamFnHook(config, customParams.prSearchFnPath, 'prSearchFn');
```

or add a `// customParams.branchNamingFnPath / customParams.prSearchFnPath` marker comment if you prefer to keep the current helper shape (regexes also match comments' text only when written as real member access — a plain comment with `customParams.branchNamingFnPath` in it does match the first regex, but the explicit-argument form above is less fragile). # gh-1039: [CRAP] configLoader.loadProjectConfig (54) + common/buildEncodedConfig.buildEncodedConfig (57)

## Description

## Problem
`js/configLoader.js::loadProjectConfig` **54.2** and `js/common/buildEncodedConfig.js::buildEncodedConfig` **57**: every agent loads project config through these. Source precedence (configPath, customParams, agentConfigsDir, defaults) must not change.

## Goal
Bring each named function under CRAP 30 by extracting pure parse/build/decide helpers and covering every branch with characterization tests. Same tracker/SCM/git/file calls in the same order.

## Acceptance
- Behaviour unchanged; each named function at or below the target; no regression; CI `crap` check green and the node harness stays green (canonical runner: `dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_all.json`).
- No code path removed; uncovered paths get a characterization test.

## Rules (read before starting)
- **Pure refactor, behaviour-preserving, backward compatible.** Same exports, same signatures, same return shapes, same log lines/side effects, same tracker/SCM calls in the same order. No config or API changes.
- **Tests first:** add characterization tests that pin the current behaviour of the paths you touch (the node harness: `dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_all.json`), then extract pure helpers (`parse*`/`build*`/`decide*`) from the big function and test those directly. Raising coverage on the function counts as much as splitting it.
- **CRAP gate:** Quality/`crap` compares this PR with the released baseline (`crap-baseline` release). The target function must go DOWN, no function may go up, new functions must be <= 8 (CRAP = CC² + CC at 0% coverage, so an untested helper needs CC <= 2 — or cover it). `crap:improved` is set automatically when it dropped. The baseline is updated by CI after the merge — do **not** commit a baseline file.
- Measure locally: `node ci/run_with_coverage.js …` then `crap4js . --coverage … --threshold 8 --baseline <released crap-baseline.json>` (see .github/workflows/quality.yml).
- Do not "fix" CRAP by deleting tests, adding `/* istanbul ignore */`, or excluding files.

## Review Threads (Inline Comments)

### Thread 1 — `js/configLoader.js` line 458

**dmtools-factory-bot** (2026-10-18):
🚨 **BLOCKING: dynamic `customParams[key]` access breaks `agentDocGenerator` static analysis → red `docs-freshness` CI**

This line is why the `docs-freshness` check is red on this head. The doc generator (`js/agentDocGenerator.js:268-269`) discovers supported `customParams` keys from JS sources with two regexes:

```javascript
/customParams\.([a-zA_$][\w$]*(?:\.[a-zA_$][\w$]*)*)/g,
/customParams\[['"]([\w.]+)['"]\]/g
```

Both only match **literal** property access. Before this PR, `configLoader.js` contained `customParams.branchNamingFnPath` and `customParams.prSearchFnPath` as static reads, so every generated agent doc listed those two keys. After the refactor, the only read is `customParams[key]` with a variable key — neither regex matches, so the keys silently vanish from the analysis.

Verified locally:
- On `origin/main`: `node js/agentDocGenerator.js` → zero diff.
- On this branch: same command → 49 generated files changed (296 deletions), all of them removing `branchNamingFnPath` / `prSearchFnPath` from the documented customParams.
- The workflow then fails at `git diff --exit-code -- docs/agents/generated` — exactly the red `docs-freshness` check in `ci_failures.md`.

Note that simply committing the regenerated docs is **not** a valid fix: those keys are still fully supported hooks (the code loads them at `js/configLoader.js:534-535`), so the regenerated docs would be wrong — they'd stop documenting live features.

**Suggested fix** — keep the two keys statically visible to the generator, e.g. read them via literal member access at the call sites:

```javascript
// instead of the generic key argument:
function loadCustomParamFnHook(target, path, exportKey) { ... }
loadCustomParamFnHook(config.git, customParams.branchNamingFnPath, 'branchNamingFn');
loadCustomParamFnHook(config, customParams.prSearchFnPath, 'prSearchFn');
```

or add a `// customParams.branchNamingFnPath / customParams.prSearchFnPath` marker comment if you prefer to keep the current helper shape (regexes also match comments' text only when written as real member access — a plain comment with `customParams.branchNamingFnPath` in it does match the first regex, but the explicit-argument form above is less fragile). # gh-1039: [CRAP] configLoader.loadProjectConfig (54) + common/buildEncodedConfig.buildEncodedConfig (57)

## Description

## Problem
`js/configLoader.js::loadProjectConfig` **54.2** and `js/common/buildEncodedConfig.js::buildEncodedConfig` **57**: every agent loads project config through these. Source precedence (configPath, customParams, agentConfigsDir, defaults) must not change.

## Goal
Bring each named function under CRAP 30 by extracting pure parse/build/decide helpers and covering every branch with characterization tests. Same tracker/SCM/git/file calls in the same order.

## Acceptance
- Behaviour unchanged; each named function at or below the target; no regression; CI `crap` check green and the node harness stays green (canonical runner: `dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_all.json`).
- No code path removed; uncovered paths get a characterization test.

## Rules (read before starting)
- **Pure refactor, behaviour-preserving, backward compatible.** Same exports, same signatures, same return shapes, same log lines/side effects, same tracker/SCM calls in the same order. No config or API changes.
- **Tests first:** add characterization tests that pin the current behaviour of the paths you touch (the node harness: `dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_all.json`), then extract pure helpers (`parse*`/`build*`/`decide*`) from the big function and test those directly. Raising coverage on the function counts as much as splitting it.
- **CRAP gate:** Quality/`crap` compares this PR with the released baseline (`crap-baseline` release). The target function must go DOWN, no function may go up, new functions must be <= 8 (CRAP = CC² + CC at 0% coverage, so an untested helper needs CC <= 2 — or cover it). `crap:improved` is set automatically when it dropped. The baseline is updated by CI after the merge — do **not** commit a baseline file.
- Measure locally: `node ci/run_with_coverage.js …` then `crap4js . --coverage … --threshold 8 --baseline <released crap-baseline.json>` (see .github/workflows/quality.yml).
- Do not "fix" CRAP by deleting tests, adding `/* istanbul ignore */`, or excluding files.

### Thread 1 — `js/configLoader.js` line 458

**dmtools-factory-bot** (2026-10-18):
🚨 **BLOCKING: dynamic `customParams[key]` access breaks `agentDocGenerator` static analysis → red `docs-freshness` CI**

This line is why the `docs-freshness` check is red on this head. The doc generator (`js/agentDocGenerator.js:268-269`) discovers supported `customParams` keys from JS sources with two regexes:

```javascript
/customParams\.([a-zA_$][\w$]*(?:\.[a-zA_$][\w$]*)*)/g,
/customParams\[['"]([\w.]+)['"]\]/g
```

Both only match **literal** property access. ### Thread 1 — `js/configLoader.js` line 458

**dmtools-factory-bot** (2026-10-18):
🚨 **BLOCKING: dynamic `customParams[key]` access breaks `agentDocGenerator` static analysis → red `docs-freshness` CI**

This line is why the `docs-freshness` check is red on this head. The doc generator (`js/agentDocGenerator.js:268-269`) discovers supported `customParams` keys from JS sources with two regexes:

```javascript
/customParams\.([a-zA_$][\w$]*(?:\.[a-zA_$][\w$]*)*)/g,
/customParams\[['"]([\w.]+)['"]\]/g
```

Both only match **literal** property access. Before this PR, `configLoader.js` contained `customParams.branchNamingFnPath` and `customParams.prSearchFnPath` as static reads, so every generated agent doc listed those two keys. After the refactor, the only read is `customParams[key]` with a variable key — neither regex matches, so the keys silently vanish from the analysis.

Verified locally:
- On `origin/main`: `node js/agentDocGenerator.js` → zero diff.
- On this branch: same command → 49 generated files changed (296 deletions), all of them removing `branchNamingFnPath` / `prSearchFnPath` from the documented customParams.
- The workflow then fails at `git diff --exit-code -- docs/agents/generated` — exactly the red `docs-freshness` check in `ci_failures.md`.

Note that simply committing the regenerated docs is **not** a valid fix: those keys are still fully supported hooks (the code loads them at `js/configLoader.js:534-535`), so the regenerated docs would be wrong — they'd stop documenting live features.

**Suggested fix** — keep the two keys statically visible to the generator, e.g. read them via literal member access at the call sites:

```javascript
// instead of the generic key argument:
function loadCustomParamFnHook(target, path, exportKey) { ... }
loadCustomParamFnHook(config.git, customParams.branchNamingFnPath, 'branchNamingFn');
loadCustomParamFnHook(config, customParams.prSearchFnPath, 'prSearchFn');
```

or add a `// customParams.branchNamingFnPath / customParams.prSearchFnPath` marker comment if you prefer to keep the current helper shape (regexes also match comments' text only when written as real member access — a plain comment with `customParams.branchNamingFnPath` in it does match the first regex, but the explicit-argument form above is less fragile). # gh-1039: [CRAP] configLoader.loadProjectConfig (54) + common/buildEncodedConfig.buildEncodedConfig (57)

## Description

## Problem
`js/configLoader.js::loadProjectConfig` **54.2** and `js/common/buildEncodedConfig.js::buildEncodedConfig` **57**: every agent loads project config through these. Source precedence (configPath, customParams, agentConfigsDir, defaults) must not change.

## Goal
Bring each named function under CRAP 30 by extracting pure parse/build/decide helpers and covering every branch with characterization tests. Same tracker/SCM/git/file calls in the same order.

## Acceptance
- Behaviour unchanged; each named function at or below the target; no regression; CI `crap` check green and the node harness stays green (canonical runner: `dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_all.json`).
- No code path removed; uncovered paths get a characterization test.

## Rules (read before starting)
- **Pure refactor, behaviour-preserving, backward compatible.** Same exports, same signatures, same return shapes, same log lines/side effects, same tracker/SCM calls in the same order. No config or API changes.
- **Tests first:** add characterization tests that pin the current behaviour of the paths you touch (the node harness: `dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_all.json`), then extract pure helpers (`parse*`/`build*`/`decide*`) from the big function and test those directly. Raising coverage on the function counts as much as splitting it.
- **CRAP gate:** Quality/`crap` compares this PR with the released baseline (`crap-baseline` release). The target function must go DOWN, no function may go up, new functions must be <= 8 (CRAP = CC² + CC at 0% coverage, so an untested helper needs CC <= 2 — or cover it). `crap:improved` is set automatically when it dropped. The baseline is updated by CI after the merge — do **not** commit a baseline file.
- Measure locally: `node ci/run_with_coverage.js …` then `crap4js . --coverage … --threshold 8 --baseline <released crap-baseline.json>` (see .github/workflows/quality.yml).
- Do not "fix" CRAP by deleting tests, adding `/* istanbul ignore */`, or excluding files.

# PR Discussion History

_Previous review discussions for PR #1056._

> ℹ️ **1 machine notice(s) excluded (arming/status boilerplate — never reply targets).**

## Review Threads (Inline Comments)

### Thread 1 — `js/configLoader.js` line 458

**dmtools-factory-bot** (2026-10-18):
🚨 **BLOCKING: dynamic `customParams[key]` access breaks `agentDocGenerator` static analysis → red `docs-freshness` CI**

This line is why the `docs-freshness` check is red on this head. The doc generator (`js/agentDocGenerator.js:268-269`) discovers supported `customParams` keys from JS sources with two regexes:

```javascript
/customParams\.([a-zA_$][\w$]*(?:\.[a-zA_$][\w$]*)*)/g,
/customParams\[['"]([\w.]+)['"]\]/g
```

Both only match **literal** property access. Before this PR, `configLoader.js` contained `customParams.branchNamingFnPath` and `customParams.prSearchFnPath` as static reads, so every generated agent doc listed those two keys. After the refactor, the only read is `customParams[key]` with a variable key — neither regex matches, so the keys silently vanish from the analysis.

Verified locally:
- On `origin/main`: `node js/agentDocGenerator.js` → zero diff.
- On this branch: same command → 49 generated files changed (296 deletions), all of them removing `branchNamingFnPath` / `prSearchFnPath` from the documented customParams.
- The workflow then fails at `git diff --exit-code -- docs/agents/generated` — exactly the red `docs-freshness` check in `ci_failures.md`.

Note that simply committing the regenerated docs is **not** a valid fix: those keys are still fully supported hooks (the code loads them at `js/configLoader.js:534-535`), so the regenerated docs would be wrong — they'd stop documenting live features.

**Suggested fix** — keep the two keys statically visible to the generator, e.g. read them via literal member access at the call sites:

```javascript
// instead of the generic key argument:
function loadCustomParamFnHook(target, path, exportKey) { ... }
loadCustomParamFnHook(config.git, customParams.branchNamingFnPath, 'branchNamingFn');
loadCustomParamFnHook(config, customParams.prSearchFnPath, 'prSearchFn');
```

or add a `// customParams.branchNamingFnPath / customParams.prSearchFnPath` marker comment if you prefer to keep the current helper shape (regexes also match comments' text only when written as real member access — a plain comment with `customParams.branchNamingFnPath` in it does match the first regex, but the explicit-argument form above is less fragile). Then re-run `node js/agentDocGenerator.js` and confirm `git diff --exit-code -- docs/agents/generated` is clean.

---

Delete the first copy.

# gh-1039: [CRAP] configLoader.loadProjectConfig (54) + common/buildEncodedConfig.buildEncodedConfig (57)

## Description

## Problem
`js/configLoader.js::loadProjectConfig` **54.2** and `js/common/buildEncodedConfig.js::buildEncodedConfig` **57**: every agent loads project config through these. Source precedence (configPath, customParams, agentConfigsDir, defaults) must not change.

## Goal
Bring each named function under CRAP 30 by extracting pure parse/build/decide helpers and covering every branch with characterization tests. Same tracker/SCM/git/file calls in the same order.

## Acceptance
- Behaviour unchanged; each named function at or below the target; no regression; CI `crap` check green and the node harness stays green (canonical runner: `dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_all.json`).
- No code path removed; uncovered paths get a characterization test.

## Rules (read before starting)
- **Pure refactor, behaviour-preserving, backward compatible.** Same exports, same signatures, same return shapes, same log lines/side effects, same tracker/SCM calls in the same order. No config or API changes.
- **Tests first:** add characterization tests that pin the current behaviour of the paths you touch (the node harness: `dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_all.json`), then extract pure helpers (`parse*`/`build*`/`decide*`) from the big function and test those directly. Raising coverage on the function counts as much as splitting it.
- **CRAP gate:** Quality/`crap` compares this PR with the released baseline (`crap-baseline` release). The target function must go DOWN, no function may go up, new functions must be <= 8 (CRAP = CC² + CC at 0% coverage, so an untested helper needs CC <= 2 — or cover it). `crap:improved` is set automatically when it dropped. The baseline is updated by CI after the merge — do **not** commit a baseline file.
- Measure locally: `node ci/run_with_coverage.js …` then `crap4js . --coverage … --threshold 8 --baseline <released crap-baseline.json>` (see .github/workflows/quality.yml).
- Do not "fix" CRAP by deleting tests, adding `/* istanbul ignore */`, or excluding files.

**dmtools-factory-bot** (2026-10-18):
🚨 **BLOCKING: dynamic `customParams[key]` access breaks `agentDocGenerator` static analysis → red `docs-freshness` CI**

This line is why the `docs-freshness` check is red on this head. The doc generator (`js/agentDocGenerator.js:268-269`) discovers supported `customParams` keys from JS sources with two regexes:

```javascript
/customParams\.([a-zA_$][\w$]*(?:\.[a-zA_$][\w$]*)*)/g,
/customParams\[['"]([\w.]+)['"]\]/g
```

Both only match **literal** property access. Before this PR, `configLoader.js` contained `customParams.branchNamingFnPath` and `customParams.prSearchFnPath` as static reads, so every generated agent doc listed those two keys. After the refactor, the only read is `customParams[key]` with a variable key — neither regex matches, so the keys silently vanish from the analysis.

Verified locally:

### Thread 1 — `js/configLoader.js` line 458

**dmtools-factory-bot** (2026-10-18):
🚨 **BLOCKING: dynamic `customParams[key]` access breaks `agentDocGenerator` static analysis → red `docs-freshness` CI**

This line is why the `docs-freshness` check is red on this head. The doc generator (`js/agentDocGenerator.js:268-269`) discovers supported `customParams` keys from JS sources with two regexes:

```javascript
/customParams\.([a-zA_$][\w$]*(?:\.[a-zA_$][\w$]*)*)/g,
/customParams\[['"]([\w.]+)['"]\]/g
```

Both only match **literal** property access. Before this PR, `configLoader.js` contained `customParams.branchNamingFnPath` and `customParams.prSearchFnPath` as static reads, so every generated agent doc listed those two keys. After the refactor, the only read is `customParams[key]` with a variable key — neither regex matches, so the keys silently vanish from the analysis.

Verified locally:
- On `origin/main`: `node js/agentDocGenerator.js` → zero diff.
- On this branch: same command → 49 generated files changed (296 deletions), all of them removing `branchNamingFnPath` / `prSearchFnPath` from the documented customParams.
- The workflow then fails at `git diff --exit-code -- docs/agents/generated` — exactly the red `docs-freshness` check in `ci_failures.md`.

Note that simply committing the regenerated docs is **not** a valid fix: those keys are still fully supported hooks (the code loads them at `js/configLoader.js:534-535`), so the regenerated docs would be wrong — they'd stop documenting live features.

**Suggested fix** — keep the two keys statically visible to the generator, e.g. read them via literal member access at the call sites:

```javascript
// instead of the generic key argument:
function loadCustomParamFnHook(target, path, exportKey) { ... }
loadCustomParamFnHook(config.git, customParams.branchNamingFnPath, 'branchNamingFn');
loadCustomParamFnHook(config, customParams.prSearchFnPath, 'prSearchFn');
```

or add a `// customParams.branchNamingFnPath / customParams.prSearchFnPath` marker comment if you prefer to keep the current helper shape (regexes also match comments' text only when written as real member access — a plain comment with `customParams.branchNamingFnPath` in it does match the first regex, but the explicit-argument form above is less fragile). # PR Discussion History

_Previous review discussions for PR #1056._

## Review Threads (Inline Comments)

### Thread 1 — `js/configLoader.js` line 458

**dmtools-factory-bot** (2026-10-18):
🚨 **BLOCKING: dynamic `customParams[key]` access breaks `agentDocGenerator` static analysis → red `docs-freshness` CI**

This line is why the `docs-freshness` check is red on this head. The doc generator (`js/agentDocGenerator.js:268-269`) discovers supported `customParams` keys from JS sources with two regexes:

```javascript
/customParams\.([a-zA_$][\w$]*(?:\.[a-zA_$][\w$]*)*)/g,
/customParams\[['"]([\w.]+)['"]\]/g
```

Both only match **literal** property access. Before this PR, `configLoader.js` contained `customParams.branchNamingFnPath` and `customParams.prSearchFnPath` as static reads, so every generated agent doc listed those two keys. After the refactor, the only read is `customParams[key]` with a variable key — neither regex matches, so the keys silently vanish from the analysis.

Verified locally:
- On `origin/main`: `node js/agentDocGenerator.js` → zero diff.
- On this branch: same command → 49 generated files changed (296 deletions), all of them removing `branchNamingFnPath` / `prSearchFnPath` from the documented customParams.
- The workflow then fails at `git diff --exit-code -- docs/agents/generated` — exactly the red `docs-freshness` check in `ci_failures.md`.

Note that simply committing the regenerated docs is **not** a valid fix: those keys are still fully supported hooks (the code loads them at `js/configLoader.js:534-535`), so the regenerated docs would be wrong — they'd stop documenting live features.

**Suggested fix** — keep the two keys statically visible to the generator, e.g. read them via literal member access at the call sites:

```javascript
// instead of the generic key argument:
function loadCustomParamFnHook(target, path, exportKey) { ... }
loadCustomParamFnHook(config.git, customParams.branchNamingFnPath, 'branchNamingFn');
loadCustomParamFnHook(config, customParams.prSearchFnPath, 'prSearchFn');
```

or add a `// customParams.branchNamingFnPath / customParams.prSearchFnPath` marker comment if you prefer to keep the current helper shape (regexes also match comments' text only when written as real member access — a plain comment with `customParams.branchNamingFnPath` in it does match the first regex, but the explicit-argument form above is less fragile). Then re-run `node js/agentDocGenerator.js` and confirm `git diff --exit-code -- docs/agents/generated` is clean.

---

# gh-1039: [CRAP] configLoader.loadProjectConfig (54) + common/buildEncodedConfig.buildEncodedConfig (57)

## Description

## Problem
`js/configLoader.js::loadProjectConfig` **54.2** and `js/common/buildEncodedConfig.js::buildEncodedConfig` **57**: every agent loads project config through these. Source precedence (configPath, customParams, agentConfigsDir, defaults) must not change.

## Goal
Bring each named function under CRAP 30 by extracting pure parse/build/decide helpers and covering every branch with characterization tests. Same tracker/SCM/git/file calls in the same order.

## Acceptance
- Behaviour unchanged; each named function at or below the target; no regression; CI `crap` check green and the node harness stays green (canonical runner: `dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_all.json`).
- No code path removed; uncovered paths get a characterization test.

## Rules (read before starting)
- **Pure refactor, behaviour-preserving, backward compatible.** Same exports, same signatures, same return shapes, same log lines/side effects, same tracker/SCM calls in the same order. No config or API changes.
- **Tests first:** add characterization tests that pin the current behaviour of the paths you touch (the node harness: `dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_all.json`), then extract pure helpers (`parse*`/`build*`/`decide*`) from the big function and test those directly. Raising coverage on the function counts as much as splitting it.
- **CRAP gate:** Quality/`crap` compares this PR with the released baseline (`crap-baseline` release). The target function must go DOWN, no function may go up, new functions must be <= 8 (CRAP = CC² + CC at 0% coverage, so an untested helper needs CC <= 2 — or cover it). `crap:improved` is set automatically when it dropped. The baseline is updated by CI after the merge — do **not** commit a baseline file.
- Measure locally: `node ci/run_with_coverage.js …` then `crap4js . --coverage … --threshold 8 --baseline <released crap-baseline.json>` (see .github/workflows/quality.yml).
- Do not "fix" CRAP by deleting tests, adding `/* istanbul ignore */`, or excluding files.

## Review Threads (Inline Comments)

### Thread 1 — `js/configLoader.js` line 458

**dmtools-factory-bot** (2026-10-18):
🚨 **BLOCKING: dynamic `customParams[key]` access breaks `agentDocGenerator` static analysis → red `docs-freshness` CI**

This line is why the `docs-freshness` check is red on this head. The doc generator (`js/agentDocGenerator.js:268-269`) discovers supported `customParams` keys from JS sources with two regexes:

```javascript
/customParams\.([a-zA_$][\w$]*(?:\.[a-zA_$][\w$]*)*)/g,
/customParams\[['"]([\w.]+)['"]\]/g
```

Both only match **literal** property access. Before this PR, `configLoader.js` contained `customParams.branchNamingFnPath` and `customParams.prSearchFnPath` as static reads, so every generated agent doc listed those two keys. After the refactor, the only read is `customParams[key]` with a variable key — neither regex matches, so the keys silently vanish from the analysis.

Verified locally:
- On `origin/main`: `node js/agentDocGenerator.js` → zero diff.
- On this branch: same command → 49 generated files changed (296 deletions), all of them removing `branchNamingFnPath` / `prSearchFnPath` from the documented customParams.
- The workflow then fails at `git diff --exit-code -- docs/agents/generated` — exactly the red `docs-freshness` check in `ci_failures.md`.

Note that simply committing the regenerated docs is **not** a valid fix: those keys are still fully supported hooks (the code loads them at `js/configLoader.js:534-535`), so the regenerated docs would be wrong — they'd stop documenting live features.

**Suggested fix** — keep the two keys statically visible to the generator, e.g. read them via literal member access at the call sites:

```javascript
// instead of the generic key argument:
function loadCustomParamFnHook(target, path, exportKey) { ... }
loadCustomParamFnHook(config.git, customParams.branchNamingFnPath, 'branchNamingFn');
loadCustomParamFnHook(config, customParams.prSearchFnPath, 'prSearchFn');
```

or add a `// customParams.branchNamingFnPath / customParams.prSearchFnPath` marker comment if you prefer to keep the current helper shape (regexes also match comments' text only when written as real member access — a plain comment with `customParams.branchNamingFnPath` in it does match the first regex, but the explicit-argument form above is less fragile). ## Description

## Problem
`js/configLoader.js::loadProjectConfig` **54.2** and `js/common/buildEncodedConfig.js::buildEncodedConfig` **57**: every agent loads project config through these. Source precedence (configPath, customParams, agentConfigsDir, defaults) must not change.

Bring each named function under CRAP 30 by extracting pure parse/build/decide helpers and covering every branch with characterization tests. Same tracker/SCM/git/file calls in the same order.

- Behaviour unchanged; each named function at or below the target; no regression; CI `crap` check green and the node harness stays green (canonical runner: `dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_all.json`).

## Rules (read before starting)
- **Pure refactor, behaviour-preserving, backward compatible.** Same exports, same signatures, same return shapes, same log lines/side effects, same tracker/SCM calls in the same order. No config or API changes.
- **Tests first:** add characterization tests that pin the current behaviour of the paths you touch (the node harness: `dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_all.json`), then extract pure helpers (`parse*`/`build*`/`decide*`) from the big function and test those directly. Raising coverage on the function counts as much as splitting it.

The target function must go DOWN, no function may go up, new functions must be <= 8 (CRAP = CC² + CC at 0% coverage, so an untested helper needs CC <= 2 — or cover it). `crap:improved` is set automatically when it dropped. The baseline is updated by CI after the merge — do **not** commit a baseline file.
- Measure locally: `node ci/run_with_coverage.js …` then `crap4js . --coverage … --threshold 8 --baseline <released crap-baseline.json>` (see .github/workflows/quality.yml).

**dmtools-factory-bot** (2026-10-18):
🚨 **BLOCKING: dynamic `customParams[key]` access breaks `agentDocGenerator` static analysis → red `docs-freshness` CI**

This line is why the `docs-freshness` check is red on this head. The doc generator (`js/agentDocGenerator.js:268-269`) discovers supported `customParams` keys from JS sources with two regexes:

```javascript
/customParams\.([a-zA_$][\w$]*(?:\.[a-zA_$][\w$]*)*)/g,
/customParams\[['"]([\w.]+)['"]\]/g
```

Both only match **literal** property access. Before this PR, `configLoader.js` contained `customParams.branchNamingFnPath` and `customParams.prSearchFnPath` as static reads, so every generated agent doc listed those two keys. After the refactor, the only read is `customParams[key]` with a variable key — neither regex matches, so the keys silently vanish from the analysis.

Verified locally:
- On `origin/main`: `node js/agentDocGenerator.js` → zero diff.
- On this branch: same command → 49 generated files changed (296 deletions), all of them removing `branchNamingFnPath` / `prSearchFnPath` from the documented customParams.
- The workflow then fails at `git diff --exit-code -- docs/agents/generated` — exactly the red `docs-freshness` check in `ci_failures.md`.

Note that simply committing the regenerated docs is **not** a valid fix: those keys are still fully supported hooks (the code loads them at `js/configLoader.js:534-535`), so the regenerated docs would be wrong — they'd stop documenting live features.

**Suggested fix** — keep the two keys statically visible to the generator, e.g. read them via literal member access at the call sites:

```javascript
// instead of the generic key argument:
function loadCustomParamFnHook(target, path, exportKey) { ... }
loadCustomParamFnHook(config.git, customParams.branchNamingFnPath, 'branchNamingFn');
loadCustomParamFnHook(config, customParams.prSearchFnPath, 'prSearchFn');
```

or add a `// customParams.branchNamingFnPath / customParams.prSearchFnPath` marker comment if you prefer to keep the current helper shape (regexes also match comments' text only when written as real member access — a plain comment with `customParams.branchNamingFnPath` in it does match the first regex, but the explicit-argument form above is less fragile). Then re-run `node js/agentDocGenerator.js` and confirm `git diff --exit-code -- docs/agents/generated` is clean.

function loadCustomParamFnHook(target, path, exportKey) { ... }

### Thread 1 — `js/configLoader.js` line 458

**dmtools-factory-bot** (2026-10-18):
🚨 **BLOCKING: dynamic `customParams[key]` access breaks `agentDocGenerator` static analysis → red `docs-freshness` CI**

This line is why the `docs-freshness` check is red on this head. The doc generator (`js/agentDocGenerator.js:268-269`) discovers supported `customParams` keys from JS sources with two regexes:

```javascript
/customParams\.([a-zA_$][\w$]*(?:\.[a-zA_$][\w$]*)*)/g,
/customParams\[['"]([\w.]+)['"]\]/g
```

Both only match **literal** property access. Before this PR, `configLoader.js` contained `customParams.branchNamingFnPath` and `customParams.prSearchFnPath` as static reads, so every generated agent doc listed those two keys. After the refactor, the only read is `customParams[key]` with a variable key — neither regex matches, so the keys silently vanish from the analysis.

Verified locally:
- On `origin/main`: `node js/agentDocGenerator.js` → zero diff.
- On this branch: same command → 49 generated files changed (296 deletions), all of them removing `branchNamingFnPath` / `prSearchFnPath` from the documented customParams.
- The workflow then fails at `git diff --exit-code -- docs/agents/generated` — exactly the red `docs-freshness` check in `ci_failures.md`.

Note that simply committing the regenerated docs is **not** a valid fix: those keys are still fully supported hooks (the code loads them at `js/configLoader.js:534-535`), so the regenerated docs would be wrong — they'd stop documenting live features.

**Suggested fix** — keep the two keys statically visible to the generator, e.g. read them via literal member access at the call sites:

```javascript
// instead of the generic key argument:
function loadCustomParamFnHook(target, path, exportKey) { ... }
loadCustomParamFnHook(config.git, customParams.branchNamingFnPath, 'branchNamingFn');
loadCustomParamFnHook(config, customParams.prSearchFnPath, 'prSearchFn');
```

or add a `// customParams.branchNamingFnPath / customParams.prSearchFnPath` marker comment if you prefer to keep the current helper shape (regexes also match comments' text only when written as real member access — a plain comment with `customParams.branchNamingFnPath` in it does match the first regex, but the explicit-argument form above is less fragile). # gh-1039: [CRAP] configLoader.loadProjectConfig (54) + common/buildEncodedConfig.buildEncodedConfig (57)

## Description

## Problem
`js/configLoader.js::loadProjectConfig` **54.2** and `js/common/buildEncodedConfig.js::buildEncodedConfig` **57**: every agent loads project config through these. Source precedence (configPath, customParams, agentConfigsDir, defaults) must not change.

## Goal
Bring each named function under CRAP 30 by extracting pure parse/build/decide helpers and covering every branch with characterization tests. Same tracker/SCM/git/file calls in the same order.

## Acceptance
- Behaviour unchanged; each named function at or below the target; no regression; CI `crap` check green and the node harness stays green (canonical runner: `dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_all.json`).
- No code path removed; uncovered paths get a characterization test.

## Rules (read before starting)
- **Pure refactor, behaviour-preserving, backward compatible.** Same exports, same signatures, same return shapes, same log lines/side effects, same tracker/SCM calls in the same order. No config or API changes.

Raising coverage on the function counts as much as splitting it.
- **CRAP gate:** Quality/`crap` compares this PR with the released baseline (`crap-baseline` release). The target function must go DOWN, no function may go up, new functions must be <= 8 (CRAP = CC² + CC at 0% coverage, so an untested helper needs CC <= 2 — or cover it). `crap:improved` is set automatically when it dropped. The baseline is updated by CI after the merge — do **not** commit a baseline file.
- Measure locally: `node ci/run_with_coverage.js …` then `crap4js . --coverage … --threshold 8 --baseline <released crap-baseline.json>` (see .github/workflows/quality.yml).
- Do not "fix" CRAP by deleting tests, adding `/* istanbul ignore */`, or excluding files.

### Thread 1 — `js/configLoader.js` line 458

**dmtools-factory-bot** (2026-10-18):
🚨 **BLOCKING: dynamic `customParams[key]` access breaks `agentDocGenerator` static analysis → red `docs-freshness` CI**

This line is why the `docs-freshness` check is red on this head. The doc generator (`js/agentDocGenerator.js:268-269`) discovers supported `customParams` keys from JS sources with two regexes:

```javascript
/customParams\.([a-zA_$][\w$]*(?:\.[a-zA_$][\w$]*)*)/g,
/customParams\[['"]([\w.]+)['"]\]/g
```

Both only match **literal** property access. Before this PR, `configLoader.js` contained `customParams.branchNamingFnPath` and `customParams.prSearchFnPath` as static reads, so every generated agent doc listed those two keys. After the refactor, the only read is `customParams[key]` with a variable key — neither regex matches, so the keys silently vanish from the analysis.

Verified locally:
- On `origin/main`: `node js/agentDocGenerator.js` → zero diff.
- On this branch: same command → 49 generated files changed (296 deletions), all of them removing `branchNamingFnPath` / `prSearchFnPath` from the documented customParams.
- The workflow then fails at `git diff --exit-code -- docs/agents/generated` — exactly the red `docs-freshness` check in `ci_failures.md`.

Note that simply committing the regenerated docs is **not** a valid fix: those keys are still fully supported hooks (the code loads them at `js/configLoader.js:534-535`), so the regenerated docs would be wrong — they'd stop documenting live features.

**Suggested fix** — keep the two keys statically visible to the generator, e.g. read them via literal member access at the call sites:

```javascript
// instead of the generic key argument:
function loadCustomParamFnHook(target, path, exportKey) { ... }
loadCustomParamFnHook(config.git, customParams.branchNamingFnPath, 'branchNamingFn');
loadCustomParamFnHook(config, customParams.prSearchFnPath, 'prSearchFn');
```

or add a `// customParams.branchNamingFnPath / customParams.prSearchFnPath` marker comment if you prefer to keep the current helper shape (regexes also match comments' text only when written as real member access — a plain comment with `customParams.branchNamingFnPath` in it does match the first regex, but the explicit-argument form above is less fragile). # gh-1039: [CRAP] configLoader.loadProjectConfig (54) + common/buildEncodedConfig.buildEncodedConfig (57)

## Description

## Problem
`js/configLoader.js::loadProjectConfig` **54.2** and `js/common/buildEncodedConfig.js::buildEncodedConfig` **57**: every agent loads project config through these. Source precedence (configPath, customParams, agentConfigsDir, defaults) must not change.

## Goal
Bring each named function under CRAP 30 by extracting pure parse/build/decide helpers and covering every branch with characterization tests. Same tracker/SCM/git/file calls in the same order.

## Acceptance
- Behaviour unchanged; each named function at or below the target; no regression; CI `crap` check green and the node harness stays green (canonical runner: `dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_all.json`).
- No code path removed; uncovered paths get a characterization test.

## Rules (read before starting)
- **Pure refactor, behaviour-preserving, backward compatible.** Same exports, same signatures, same return shapes, same log lines/side effects, same tracker/SCM calls in the same order. No config or API changes.
- **Tests first:** add characterization tests that pin the current behaviour of the paths you touch (the node harness: `dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_all.json`), then extract pure helpers (`parse*`/`build*`/`decide*`) from the big function and test those directly. Raising coverage on the function counts as much as splitting it.
- **CRAP gate:** Quality/`crap` compares this PR with the released baseline (`crap-baseline` release). The target function must go DOWN, no function may go up, new functions must be <= 8 (CRAP = CC² + CC at 0% coverage, so an untested helper needs CC <= 2 — or cover it). `crap:improved` is set automatically when it dropped. The baseline is updated by CI after the merge — do **not** commit a baseline file.
- Measure locally: `node ci/run_with_coverage.js …` then `crap4js . --coverage … --threshold 8 --baseline <released crap-baseline.json>` (see .github/workflows/quality.yml).
- Do not "fix" CRAP by deleting tests, adding `/* istanbul ignore */`, or excluding files.

## Review Threads (Inline Comments)

### Thread 1 — `js/configLoader.js` line 458

**dmtools-factory-bot** (2026-10-18):
🚨 **BLOCKING: dynamic `customParams[key]` access breaks `agentDocGenerator` static analysis → red `docs-freshness` CI**

This line is why the `docs-freshness` check is red on this head. The doc generator (`js/agentDocGenerator.js:268-269`) discovers supported `customParams` keys from JS sources with two regexes:

```javascript
/customParams\.([a-zA_$][\w$]*(?:\.[a-zA_$][\w$]*)*)/g,
/customParams\[['"]([\w.]+)['"]\]/g
```

Both only match **literal** property access. Before this PR, `configLoader.js` contained `customParams.branchNamingFnPath` and `customParams.prSearchFnPath` as static reads, so every generated agent doc listed those two keys. After the refactor, the only read is `customParams[key]` with a variable key — neither regex matches, so the keys silently vanish from the analysis.

Verified locally:
- On `origin/main`: `node js/agentDocGenerator.js` → zero diff.
- On this branch: same command → 49 generated files changed (296 deletions), all of them removing `branchNamingFnPath` / `prSearchFnPath` from the documented customParams.
- The workflow then fails at `git diff --exit-code -- docs/agents/generated` — exactly the red `docs-freshness` check in `ci_failures.md`.

Note that simply committing the regenerated docs is **not** a valid fix: those keys are still fully supported hooks (the code loads them at `js/configLoader.js:534-535`), so the regenerated docs would be wrong — they'd stop documenting live features.

**Suggested fix** — keep the two keys statically visible to the generator, e.g. read them via literal member access at the call sites:

```javascript
// instead of the generic key argument:
function loadCustomParamFnHook(target, path, exportKey) { ... }
loadCustomParamFnHook(config.git, customParams.branchNamingFnPath, 'branchNamingFn');
loadCustomParamFnHook(config, customParams.prSearchFnPath, 'prSearchFn');
```

or add a `// customParams.branchNamingFnPath / customParams.prSearchFnPath` marker comment if you prefer to keep the current helper shape (regexes also match comments' text only when written as real member access — a plain comment with `customParams.branchNamingFnPath` in it does match the first regex, but the explicit-argument form above is less fragile). # gh-1039: [CRAP] configLoader.loadProjectConfig (54) + common/buildEncodedConfig.buildEncodedConfig (57)

## Description

## Problem
`js/configLoader.js::loadProjectConfig` **54.2** and `js/common/buildEncodedConfig.js::buildEncodedConfig` **57**: every agent loads project config through these. Source precedence (configPath, customParams, agentConfigsDir, defaults) must not change.

## Goal
Bring each named function under CRAP 30 by extracting pure parse/build/decide helpers and covering every branch with characterization tests. Same tracker/SCM/git/file calls in the same order.

## Acceptance
- Behaviour unchanged; each named function at or below the target; no regression; CI `crap` check green and the node harness stays green (canonical runner: `dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_all.json`).
- No code path removed; uncovered paths get a characterization test.

## Rules (read before starting)
- **Pure refactor, behaviour-preserving, backward compatible.** Same exports, same signatures, same return shapes, same log lines/side effects, same tracker/SCM calls in the same order. No config or API changes.
- **Tests first:** add characterization tests that pin the current behaviour of the paths you touch (the node harness: `dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_all.json`), then extract pure helpers (`parse*`/`build*`/`decide*`) from the big function and test those directly. Raising coverage on the function counts as much as splitting it.
- **CRAP gate:** Quality/`crap` compares this PR with the released baseline (`crap-baseline` release). The target function must go DOWN, no function may go up, new functions must be <= 8 (CRAP = CC² + CC at 0% coverage, so an untested helper needs CC <= 2 — or cover it). `crap:improved` is set automatically when it dropped. The baseline is updated by CI after the merge — do **not** commit a baseline file.
- Measure locally: `node ci/run_with_coverage.js …` then `crap4js . --coverage … --threshold 8 --baseline <released crap-baseline.json>` (see .github/workflows/quality.yml).
- Do not "fix" CRAP by deleting tests, adding `/* istanbul ignore */`, or excluding files.

# PR Discussion History

_Previous review discussions for PR #1056._

## Review Threads (Inline Comments)

### Thread 1 — `js/configLoader.js` line 458

**dmtools-factory-bot** (2026-10-18):
🚨 **BLOCKING: dynamic `customParams[key]` access breaks `agentDocGenerator` static analysis → red `docs-freshness` CI**

This line is why the `docs-freshness` check is red on this head. The doc generator (`js/agentDocGenerator.js:268-269`) discovers supported `customParams` keys from JS sources with two regexes:

```javascript
/customParams\.([a-zA_$][\w$]*(?:\.[a-zA_$][\w$]*)*)/g,
/customParams\[['"]([\w.]+)['"]\]/g
```

Both only match **literal** property access. Before this PR, `configLoader.js` contained `customParams.branchNamingFnPath` and `customParams.prSearchFnPath` as static reads, so every generated agent doc listed those two keys. After the refactor, the only read is `customParams[key]` with a variable key — neither regex matches, so the keys silently vanish from the analysis.

Verified locally:
- On `origin/main`: `node js/agentDocGenerator.js` → zero diff.
- On this branch: same command → 49 generated files changed (296 deletions), all of them removing `branchNamingFnPath` / `prSearchFnPath` from the documented customParams.
- The workflow then fails at `git diff --exit-code -- docs/agents/generated` — exactly the red `docs-freshness` check in `ci_failures.md`.

Note that simply committing the regenerated docs is **not** a valid fix: those keys are still fully supported hooks (the code loads them at `js/configLoader.js:534-535`), so the regenerated docs would be wrong — they'd stop documenting live features.

**Suggested fix** — keep the two keys statically visible to the generator, e.g. read them via literal member access at the call sites:

```javascript
// instead of the generic key argument:
function loadCustomParamFnHook(target, path, exportKey) { ... }
loadCustomParamFnHook(config.git, customParams.branchNamingFnPath, 'branchNamingFn');
loadCustomParamFnHook(config, customParams.prSearchFnPath, 'prSearchFn');
```

or add a `// customParams.branchNamingFnPath / customParams.prSearchFnPath` marker comment if you prefer to keep the current helper shape (regexes also match comments' text only when written as real member access — a plain comment with `customParams.branchNamingFnPath` in it does match the first regex, but the explicit-argument form above is less fragile). Then re-run `node js/agentDocGenerator.js` and confirm `git diff --exit-code -- docs/agents/generated` is clean.

# gh-1039: [CRAP] configLoader.loadProjectConfig (54) + common/buildEncodedConfig.buildEncodedConfig (57)

## Description

## Problem
`js/configLoader.js::loadProjectConfig` **54.2** and `js/common/buildEncodedConfig.js::buildEncodedConfig` **57**: every agent loads project config through these. Source precedence (configPath, customParams, agentConfigsDir, defaults) must not change.

## Goal
Bring each named function under CRAP 30 by extracting pure parse/build/decide helpers and covering every branch with characterization tests. Same tracker/SCM/git/file calls in the same order.

## Acceptance
- Behaviour unchanged; each named function at or below the target; no regression; CI `crap` check green and the node harness stays green (canonical runner: `dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_all.json`).
- No code path removed; uncovered paths get a characterization test.

## Rules (read before starting)
- **Pure refactor, behaviour-preserving, backward compatible.** Same exports, same signatures, same return shapes, same log lines/side effects, same tracker/SCM calls in the same order. No config or API changes.
- **Tests first:** add characterization tests that pin the current behaviour of the paths you touch (the node harness: `dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_all.json`), then extract pure helpers (`parse*`/`build*`/`decide*`) from the big function and test those directly. Raising coverage on the function counts as much as splitting it.
- **CRAP gate:** Quality/`crap` compares this PR with the released baseline (`crap-baseline` release). The target function must go DOWN, no function may go up, new functions must be <= 8 (CRAP = CC² + CC at 0% coverage, so an untested helper needs CC <= 2 — or cover it). `crap:improved` is set automatically when it dropped. The baseline is updated by CI after the merge — do **not** commit a baseline file.
- Measure locally: `node ci/run_with_coverage.js …` then `crap4js . --coverage … --threshold 8 --baseline <released crap-baseline.json>` (see .github/workflows/quality.yml).
- Do not "fix" CRAP by deleting tests, adding `/* istanbul ignore */`, or excluding files.

# PR Discussion History

_Previous review discussions for PR #1056._

> ℹ️ **1 machine notice(s) excluded (arming/status boilerplate — never reply targets).**

## Review Threads (Inline Comments)

### Thread 1 — `js/configLoader.js` line 458

**dmtools-factory-bot** (2026-10-18):
🚨 **BLOCKING: dynamic `customParams[key]` access breaks `agentDocGenerator` static analysis → red `docs-freshness` CI**

This line is why the `docs-freshness` check is red on this head. The doc generator (`js/agentDocGenerator.js:268-269`) discovers supported `customParams` keys from JS sources with two regexes:

```javascript
/customParams\.([a-zA_$][\w$]*(?:\.[a-zA_$][\w$]*)*)/g,
/customParams\[['"]([\w.]+)['"]\]/g
```

Both only match **literal** property access. Before this PR, `configLoader.js` contained `customParams.branchNamingFnPath` and `customParams.prSearchFnPath` as static reads, so every generated agent doc listed those two keys. After the refactor, the only read is `customParams[key]` with a variable key — neither regex matches, so the keys silently vanish from the analysis.

Verified locally:
- On `origin/main`: `node js/agentDocGenerator.js` → zero diff.
- On this branch: same command → 49 generated files changed (296 deletions), all of them removing `branchNamingFnPath` / `prSearchFnPath` from the documented customParams.
- The workflow then fails at `git diff --exit-code -- docs/agents/generated` — exactly the red `docs-freshness` check in `ci_failures.md`.

Note that simply committing the regenerated docs is **not** a valid fix: those keys are still fully supported hooks (the code loads them at `js/configLoader.js:534-535`), so the regenerated docs would be wrong — they'd stop documenting live features.

**Suggested fix** — keep the two keys statically visible to the generator, e.g. read them via literal member access at the call sites:

```javascript
// instead of the generic key argument:
function loadCustomParamFnHook(target, path, exportKey) { ... }
loadCustomParamFnHook(config.git, customParams.branchNamingFnPath, 'branchNamingFn');
loadCustomParamFnHook(config, customParams.prSearchFnPath, 'prSearchFn');
```

or add a `// customParams.branchNamingFnPath / customParams.prSearchFnPath` marker comment if you prefer to keep the current helper shape (regexes also match comments' text only when written as real member access — a plain comment with `customParams.branchNamingFnPath` in it does match the first regex, but the explicit-argument form above is less fragile). Then re-run `node js/agentDocGenerator.js` and confirm `git diff --exit-code -- docs/agents/generated` is clean.

---

Delete the first copy.

# gh-1039: [CRAP] configLoader.loadProjectConfig (54) + common/buildEncodedConfig.buildEncodedConfig (57)

## Description

## Problem
`js/configLoader.js::loadProjectConfig` **54.2** and `js/common/buildEncodedConfig.js::buildEncodedConfig` **57**: every agent loads project config through these. Source precedence (configPath, customParams, agentConfigsDir, defaults) must not change.

## Goal
Bring each named function under CRAP 30 by extracting pure parse/build/decide helpers and covering every branch with characterization tests. Same tracker/SCM/git/file calls in the same order.

## Acceptance
- Behaviour unchanged; each named function at or below the target; no regression; CI `crap` check green and the node harness stays green (canonical runner: `dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_all.json`).
- No code path removed; uncovered paths get a characterization test.

## Rules (read before starting)
- **Pure refactor, behaviour-preserving, backward compatible.** Same exports, same signatures, same return shapes, same log lines/side effects, same tracker/SCM calls in the same order. No config or API changes.
- **Tests first:** add characterization tests that pin the current behaviour of the paths you touch (the node harness: `dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_all.json`), then extract pure helpers (`parse*`/`build*`/`decide*`) from the big function and test those directly. Raising coverage on the function counts as much as splitting it.
- **CRAP gate:** Quality/`crap` compares this PR with the released baseline (`crap-baseline` release). The target function must go DOWN, no function may go up, new functions must be <= 8 (CRAP = CC² + CC at 0% coverage, so an untested helper needs CC <= 2 — or cover it). `crap:improved` is set automatically when it dropped. The baseline is updated by CI after the merge — do **not** commit a baseline file.
- Measure locally: `node ci/run_with_coverage.js …` then `crap4js . --coverage … --threshold 8 --baseline <released crap-baseline.json>` (see .github/workflows/quality.yml).
- Do not "fix" CRAP by deleting tests, adding `/* istanbul ignore */`, or excluding files.

## Review Threads (Inline Comments)

### Thread 1 — `js/configLoader.js` line 458

**dmtools-factory-bot** (2026-10-18):
🚨 **BLOCKING: dynamic `customParams[key]` access breaks `agentDocGenerator` static analysis → red `docs-freshness` CI**

This line is why the `docs-freshness` check is red on this head. The doc generator (`js/agentDocGenerator.js:268-269`) discovers supported `customParams` keys from JS sources with two regexes:

```javascript
/customParams\.([a-zA_$][\w$]*(?:\.[a-zA_$][\w$]*)*)/g,
/customParams\[['"]([\w.]+)['"]\]/g
```

Both only match **literal** property access. Before this PR, `configLoader.js` contained `customParams.branchNamingFnPath` and `customParams.prSearchFnPath` as static reads, so every generated agent doc listed those two keys. After the refactor, the only read is `customParams[key]` with a variable key — neither regex matches, so the keys silently vanish from the analysis.

Verified locally:
- On `origin/main`: `node js/agentDocGenerator.js` → zero diff.
- On this branch: same command → 49 generated files changed (296 deletions), all of them removing `branchNamingFnPath` / `prSearchFnPath` from the documented customParams.
- The workflow then fails at `git diff --exit-code -- docs/agents/generated` — exactly the red `docs-freshness` check in `ci_failures.md`.

Note that simply committing the regenerated docs is **not** a valid fix: those keys are still fully supported hooks (the code loads them at `js/configLoader.js:534-535`), so the regenerated docs would be wrong — they'd stop documenting live features.

**Suggested fix** — keep the two keys statically visible to the generator, e.g. read them via literal member access at the call sites:

```javascript
// instead of the generic key argument:
function loadCustomParamFnHook(target, path, exportKey) { ... }
loadCustomParamFnHook(config.git, customParams.branchNamingFnPath, 'branchNamingFn');
loadCustomParamFnHook(config, customParams.prSearchFnPath, 'prSearchFn');
```

or add a `// customParams.branchNamingFnPath / customParams.prSearchFnPath` marker comment if you prefer to keep the current helper shape (regexes also match comments' text only when written as real member access — a plain comment with `customParams.branchNamingFnPath` in it does match the first regex, but the explicit-argument form above is less fragile). # gh-1039: [CRAP] configLoader.loadProjectConfig (54) + common/buildEncodedConfig.buildEncodedConfig (57)

## Description

## Problem
`js/configLoader.js::loadProjectConfig` **54.2** and `js/common/buildEncodedConfig.js::buildEncodedConfig` **57**: every agent loads project config through these. Source precedence (configPath, customParams, agentConfigsDir, defaults) must not change.

## Goal
Bring each named function under CRAP 30 by extracting pure parse/build/decide helpers and covering every branch with characterization tests. Same tracker/SCM/git/file calls in the same order.

## Acceptance
- Behaviour unchanged; each named function at or below the target; no regression; CI `crap` check green and the node harness stays green (canonical runner: `dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_all.json`).
- No code path removed; uncovered paths get a characterization test.

## Rules (read before starting)
- **Pure refactor, behaviour-preserving, backward compatible.** Same exports, same signatures, same return shapes, same log lines/side effects, same tracker/SCM calls in the same order. No config or API changes.
- **Tests first:** add characterization tests that pin the current behaviour of the paths you touch (the node harness: `dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_all.json`), then extract pure helpers (`parse*`/`build*`/`decide*`) from the big function and test those directly. Raising coverage on the function counts as much as splitting it.
- **CRAP gate:** Quality/`crap` compares this PR with the released baseline (`crap-baseline` release). The target function must go DOWN, no function may go up, new functions must be <= 8 (CRAP = CC² + CC at 0% coverage, so an untested helper needs CC <= 2 — or cover it). `crap:improved` is set automatically when it dropped. The baseline is updated by CI after the merge — do **not** commit a baseline file.
- Measure locally: `node ci/run_with_coverage.js …` then `crap4js . --coverage … --threshold 8 --baseline <released crap-baseline.json>` (see .github/workflows/quality.yml).
- Do not "fix" CRAP by deleting tests, adding `/* istanbul ignore */`, or excluding files.

# PR Discussion History

_Previous review discussions for PR #1056._

> ℹ️ **1 machine notice(s) excluded (arming/status boilerplate — never reply targets).**

## Review Threads (Inline Comments)

### Thread 1 — `js/configLoader.js` line 458

**dmtools-factory-bot** (2026-10-18):
🚨 **BLOCKING: dynamic `customParams[key]` access breaks `agentDocGenerator` static analysis → red `docs-freshness` CI**

This line is why the `docs-freshness` check is red on this head. The doc generator (`js/agentDocGenerator.js:268-269`) discovers supported `customParams` keys from JS sources with two regexes:

```javascript
/customParams\.([a-zA_$][\w$]*(?:\.[a-zA_$][\w$]*)*)/g,
/customParams\[['"]([\w.]+)['"]\]/g
```

Both only match **literal** property access. Before this PR, `configLoader.js` contained `customParams.branchNamingFnPath` and `customParams.prSearchFnPath` as static reads, so every generated agent doc listed those two keys. After the refactor, the only read is `customParams[key]` with a variable key — neither regex matches, so the keys silently vanish from the analysis.

Verified locally:
- On `origin/main`: `node js/agentDocGenerator.js` → zero diff.
- On this branch: same command → 49 generated files changed (296 deletions), all of them removing `branchNamingFnPath` / `prSearchFnPath` from the documented customParams.
- The workflow then fails at `git diff --exit-code -- docs/agents/generated` — exactly the red `docs-freshness` check in `ci_failures.md`.

Note that simply committing the regenerated docs is **not** a valid fix: those keys are still fully supported hooks (the code loads them at `js/configLoader.js:534-535`), so the regenerated docs would be wrong — they'd stop documenting live features.

**Suggested fix** — keep the two keys statically visible to the generator, e.g. read them via literal member access at the call sites:

```javascript
// instead of the generic key argument:
function loadCustomParamFnHook(target, path, exportKey) { ... }
loadCustomParamFnHook(config.git, customParams.branchNamingFnPath, 'branchNamingFn');
loadCustomParamFnHook(config, customParams.prSearchFnPath, 'prSearchFn');
```

or add a `// customParams.branchNamingFnPath / customParams.prSearchFnPath` marker comment if you prefer to keep the current helper shape (regexes also match comments' text only when written as real member access — a plain comment with `customParams.branchNamingFnPath` in it does match the first regex, but the explicit-argument form above is less fragile). Then re-run `node js/agentDocGenerator.js` and confirm `git diff --exit-code -- docs/agents/generated` is clean.

---

Delete the first copy.

# gh-1039: [CRAP] configLoader.loadProjectConfig (54) + common/buildEncodedConfig.buildEncodedConfig (57)

## Description

## Problem
`js/configLoader.js::loadProjectConfig` **54.2** and `js/common/buildEncodedConfig.js::buildEncodedConfig` **57**: every agent loads project config through these. Source precedence (configPath, customParams, agentConfigsDir, defaults) must not change.

## Goal
Bring each named function under CRAP 30 by extracting pure parse/build/decide helpers and covering every branch with characterization tests. Same tracker/SCM/git/file calls in the same order.

## Acceptance
- Behaviour unchanged; each named function at or below the target; no regression; CI `crap` check green and the node harness stays green (canonical runner: `dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_all.json`).
- No code path removed; uncovered paths get a characterization test.

## Rules (read before starting)
- **Pure refactor, behaviour-preserving, backward compatible.** Same exports, same signatures, same return shapes, same log lines/side effects, same tracker/SCM calls in the same order. No config or API changes.
- **Tests first:** add characterization tests that pin the current behaviour of the paths you touch (the node harness: `dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_all.json`), then extract pure helpers (`parse*`/`build*`/`decide*`) from the big function and test those directly. Raising coverage on the function counts as much as splitting it.
- **CRAP gate:** Quality/`crap` compares this PR with the released baseline (`crap-baseline` release). The target function must go DOWN, no function may go up, new functions must be <= 8 (CRAP = CC² + CC at 0% coverage, so an untested helper needs CC <= 2 — or cover it). `crap:improved` is set automatically when it dropped. The baseline is updated by CI after the merge — do **not** commit a baseline file.
- Measure locally: `node ci/run_with_coverage.js …` then `crap4js . --coverage … --threshold 8 --baseline <released crap-baseline.json>` (see .github/workflows/quality.yml).
- Do not "fix" CRAP by deleting tests, adding `/* istanbul ignore */`, or excluding files.
