**dmtools-factory-bot** (2026-10-18):
🚨 **BLOCKING: dynamic `customParams[key]` access breaks `agentDocGenerator` static analysis → red `docs-freshness` CI**

This line is why the `docs-freshness` check is red on this head. The doc generator (`js/agentDocGenerator.js:268-269`) discovers supported `customParams` keys from JS sources with two regexes:

```javascript
/customParams\.([a-zA_$][\w$]*(?:\.[a-zA_$][\w$]*)*)/g,
/customParams\[['"]([\w.]+)['"]\]/g
```

Both only match **literal** property access. Before this PR, `configLoader.js` contained `customParams.branchNamingFnPath` and `customParams.prSearchFnPath` as static reads, so every generated agent doc listed those two keys. After the refactor, the only read is `customParams[key]` with a variable key — neither regex matches, so the keys silently vanish from the analysis.

Verified locally:
- On `origin/main`: `node js/agentDocGenerator.js` → zero diff.
- On this branch: same command → 49 generated files changed (296 deletions), all of them removing `branchNamingFnPath` / `prSearchFnPath` from the documented customParams.
- The workflow then fails at `git diff --exit-code -- docs/agents/generated` — exactly the red `docs-freshness` check in `ci_failures.md`.

Note that simply committing the regenerated docs is **not** a valid fix: those keys are still fully supported hooks (the code loads them at `js/configLoader.js:534-535`), so the regenerated docs would be wrong — they'd stop documenting live features.

**Suggested fix** — keep the two keys statically visible to the generator, e.g. read them via literal member access at the call sites:

```javascript
// instead of the generic key argument:
function loadCustomParamFnHook(target, path, exportKey) { ... }
loadCustomParamFnHook(config.git, customParams.branchNamingFnPath, 'branchNamingFn');
loadCustomParamFnHook(config, customParams.prSearchFnPath, 'prSearchFn');
```

or add a `// customParams.branchNamingFnPath / customParams.prSearchFnPath` marker comment if you prefer to keep the current helper shape (regexes also match comments' text only when written as real member access — a plain comment with `customParams.branchNamingFnPath` in it does match the first regex, but the explicit-argument form above is less fragile). # Re: dynamic `customParams[key]` breaks agentDocGenerator static analysis

Fixed. `loadCustomParamFnHook` no longer reads the hook path via a dynamic `customParams[key]` lookup. The signature is now `loadCustomParamFnHook(target, path, key, exportKey)` and the two call sites in `loadProjectConfig` pass the paths as **literal** member reads:

```javascript
loadCustomParamFnHook(config.git, customParams.branchNamingFnPath, 'branchNamingFnPath', 'branchNamingFn');
loadCustomParamFnHook(config, customParams.prSearchFnPath, 'prSearchFnPath', 'prSearchFn');
```

Both `customParams.branchNamingFnPath` and `customParams.prSearchFnPath` literal accesses are now visible to the two regexes in `js/agentDocGenerator.js:268-269`, so the keys stay in every generated agent doc (the hooks remain fully supported features — committing regenerated docs would have been wrong).

Verified:
- `node js/agentDocGenerator.js` → exit 0, `git diff --exit-code -- docs/agents/generated` → clean (0 changed files; previously 49 files / 296 deletions on this head).
- Behaviour unchanged: identical log/warn lines (the `key` argument preserves the exact warn wording), same loader, same install targets.
- New regression tests in `js/unit-tests/test_configLoader.js`: a suite pinning that `configLoader.js` keeps both keys discoverable by the agentDocGenerator literal regexes, plus direct unit tests of `loadCustomParamFnHook` (loads function, no-op on falsy path, warns on non-function export).

# Re: duplicated / orphaned `buildEncodedConfig` JSDoc block

Fixed. Deleted the orphaned copy of the `buildEncodedConfig` docblock (`Build the encoded config payload for a workflow dispatch.…`) that sat above `resolveProjectKey`; the full docblock now appears exactly once, directly above the real `buildEncodedConfig` function.

Also fixed the minor note: removed the stray double blank line after the closing `}` of `loadProjectConfig` in `js/configLoader.js`.

A regression test in `js/unit-tests/test_buildEncodedConfig.js` pins the JSDoc summary to appear exactly once in the source, so the orphaned duplicate cannot silently come back.

# PR Discussion History

_Previous review discussions for PR #1056._

> ℹ️ **1 machine notice(s) excluded (arming/status boilerplate — never reply targets).**

## Review Threads (Inline Comments)

### Thread 1 — `js/configLoader.js` line 458

**dmtools-factory-bot** (2026-10-18):
🚨 **BLOCKING: dynamic `customParams[key]` access breaks `agentDocGenerator` static analysis → red `docs-freshness` CI**

This line is why the `docs-freshness` check is red on this head. The doc generator (`js/agentDocGenerator.js:268-269`) discovers supported `customParams` keys from JS sources with two regexes:

```javascript
/customParams\.([a-zA_$][\w$]*(?:\.[a-zA_$][\w$]*)*)/g,
/customParams\[['"]([\w.]+)['"]\]/g
```

Both only match **literal** property access. Before this PR, `configLoader.js` contained `customParams.branchNamingFnPath` and `customParams.prSearchFnPath` as static reads, so every generated agent doc listed those two keys. After the refactor, the only read is `customParams[key]` with a variable key — neither regex matches, so the keys silently vanish from the analysis.

Verified locally:
- On `origin/main`: `node js/agentDocGenerator.js` → zero diff.
- On this branch: same command → 49 generated files changed (296 deletions), all of them removing `branchNamingFnPath` / `prSearchFnPath` from the documented customParams.
- The workflow then fails at `git diff --exit-code -- docs/agents/generated` — exactly the red `docs-freshness` check in `ci_failures.md`.

Note that simply committing the regenerated docs is **not** a valid fix: those keys are still fully supported hooks (the code loads them at `js/configLoader.js:534-535`), so the regenerated docs would be wrong — they'd stop documenting live features.

**Suggested fix** — keep the two keys statically visible to the generator, e.g. read them via literal member access at the call sites:

```javascript
// instead of the generic key argument:
function loadCustomParamFnHook(target, path, exportKey) { ... }
loadCustomParamFnHook(config.git, customParams.branchNamingFnPath, 'branchNamingFn');
loadCustomParamFnHook(config, customParams.prSearchFnPath, 'prSearchFn');
```

or add a `// customParams.branchNamingFnPath / customParams.prSearchFnPath` marker comment if you prefer to keep the current helper shape (regexes also match comments' text only when written as real member access — a plain comment with `customParams.branchNamingFnPath` in it does match the first regex, but the explicit-argument form above is less fragile). Then re-run `node js/agentDocGenerator.js` and confirm `git diff --exit-code -- docs/agents/generated` is clean.

# gh-1039: [CRAP] configLoader.loadProjectConfig (54) + common/buildEncodedConfig.buildEncodedConfig (57)

## Description

## Problem
`js/configLoader.js::loadProjectConfig` **54.2** and `js/common/buildEncodedConfig.js::buildEncodedConfig` **57**: every agent loads project config through these. Source precedence (configPath, customParams, agentConfigsDir, defaults) must not change.

## Goal
Bring each named function under CRAP 30 by extracting pure parse/build/decide helpers and covering every branch with characterization tests. Same tracker/SCM/git/file calls in the same order.

## Acceptance
- Behaviour unchanged; each named function at or below the target; no regression; CI `crap` check green and the node harness stays green (canonical runner: `dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_all.json`).
- No code path removed; uncovered paths get a characterization test.

## Rules (read before starting)
- **Pure refactor, behaviour-preserving, backward compatible.** Same exports, same signatures, same return shapes, same log lines/side effects, same tracker/SCM calls in the same order. No config or API changes.
- **Tests first:** add characterization tests that pin the current behaviour of the paths you touch (the node harness: `dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_all.json`), then extract pure helpers (`parse*`/`build*`/`decide*`) from the big function and test those directly. Raising coverage on the function counts as much as splitting it.
- **CRAP gate:** Quality/`crap` compares this PR with the released baseline (`crap-baseline` release). The target function must go DOWN, no function may go up, new functions must be <= 8 (CRAP = CC² + CC at 0% coverage, so an untested helper needs CC <= 2 — or cover it). `crap:improved` is set automatically when it dropped. The baseline is updated by CI after the merge — do **not** commit a baseline file.
- Measure locally: `node ci/run_with_coverage.js …` then `crap4js . --coverage … --threshold 8 --baseline <released crap-baseline.json>` (see .github/workflows/quality.yml).
- Do not "fix" CRAP by deleting tests, adding `/* istanbul ignore */`, or excluding files.

# gh-1039: [CRAP] configLoader.loadProjectConfig (54) + common/buildEncodedConfig.buildEncodedConfig (57)

## Description

## Problem
`js/configLoader.js::loadProjectConfig` **54.2** and `js/common/buildEncodedConfig.js::buildEncodedConfig` **57**: every agent loads project config through these. Source precedence (configPath, customParams, agentConfigsDir, defaults) must not change.

## Goal
Bring each named function under CRAP 30 by extracting pure parse/build/decide helpers and covering every branch with characterization tests. Same tracker/SCM/git/file calls in the same order.

## Acceptance
- Behaviour unchanged; each named function at or below the target; no regression; CI `crap` check green and the node harness stays green (canonical runner: `dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_all.json`).
- No code path removed; uncovered paths get a characterization test.

## Rules (read before starting)
- **Pure refactor, behaviour-preserving, backward compatible.** Same exports, same signatures, same return shapes, same log lines/side effects, same tracker/SCM calls in the same order. No config or API changes.
- **Tests first:** add characterization tests that pin the current behaviour of the paths you touch (the node harness: `dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_all.json`), then extract pure helpers (`parse*`/`build*`/`decide*`) from the big function and test those directly. Raising coverage on the function counts as much as splitting it.
- **CRAP gate:** Quality/`crap` compares this PR with the released baseline (`crap-baseline` release). The target function must go DOWN, no function may go up, new functions must be <= 8 (CRAP = CC² + CC at 0% coverage, so an untested helper needs CC <= 2 — or cover it). `crap:improved` is set automatically when it dropped. The baseline is updated by CI after the merge — do **not** commit a baseline file.
- Measure locally: `node ci/run_with_coverage.js …` then `crap4js . --coverage … --threshold 8 --baseline <released crap-baseline.json>` (see .github/workflows/quality.yml).
- Do not "fix" CRAP by deleting tests, adding `/* istanbul ignore */`, or excluding files.

# Rework — gh-1039 (PR #1056)

## Issues/Notes

- 🚨 **`docs-freshness` CI red** (root cause, confirmed locally): the new `loadCustomParamFnHook` read hooks via dynamic `customParams[key]`, which the two literal-access regexes in `js/agentDocGenerator.js` cannot see — `branchNamingFnPath` / `prSearchFnPath` silently vanished from all 49 generated agent docs (296 deletions) and the freshness gate failed at `git diff --exit-code -- docs/agents/generated`. Committing regenerated docs was not an option: both hooks remain live features.
- 💡 Orphaned duplicate of the `buildEncodedConfig` JSDoc block above `resolveProjectKey`, plus a stray double blank line after `loadProjectConfig`.

## Approach

TDD (RED → GREEN) for every change:

1. **RED** — added failing tests reproducing each finding:
   - `test_configLoader.js`: a suite asserting the real `js/configLoader.js` source keeps `branchNamingFnPath` / `prSearchFnPath` discoverable by the exact `agentDocGenerator` literal regexes, plus direct unit tests of `loadCustomParamFnHook` with the new explicit-path signature (loads function / no-op on falsy path / warns on non-function export).
   - `test_buildEncodedConfig.js`: a test pinning the `buildEncodedConfig` JSDoc summary to appear exactly once in the source.
   - Result: 4 new tests failed exactly as the review predicted.
2. **GREEN** — minimal code changes:
   - `js/configLoader.js`: `loadCustomParamFnHook(target, customParams, key, exportKey)` → `loadCustomParamFnHook(target, path, key, exportKey)`; call sites now pass literal member reads (`customParams.branchNamingFnPath`, `customParams.prSearchFnPath`), keeping both keys statically visible to the doc generator. The `key` argument preserves the exact warn log line; loader, install targets, and all other log lines unchanged. Also removed the stray double blank line after `loadProjectConfig`.
   - `js/common/buildEncodedConfig.js`: deleted the orphaned duplicated docblock; the full JSDoc now sits exactly once above the real `buildEncodedConfig`.
3. **Verified the actual gate**: `node js/agentDocGenerator.js` regenerates with **zero diff** (`git diff --exit-code -- docs/agents/generated` → clean) — previously 49 changed files on this head.

## Files Modified

- `js/configLoader.js` — `loadCustomParamFnHook` signature/call sites (literal `customParams` reads); stray blank line removed.
- `js/common/buildEncodedConfig.js` — orphaned duplicated JSDoc deleted.
- `js/unit-tests/test_configLoader.js` — `loadCustomParamFnHook` unit tests + agentDocGenerator static-visibility contract test.
- `js/unit-tests/test_buildEncodedConfig.js` — single-docblock regression test.

## Test Coverage

- Full canonical suite: `dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_all.json` → **4335 passed, 0 failed**.
- Targeted suites (`test_configLoader.js`, `test_buildEncodedConfig.js`): 173 passed, 0 failed (4 new tests; all failed RED before the fix).
- `node js/agentDocGenerator.js` → exit 0; `git diff --exit-code -- docs/agents/generated` → clean (docs-freshness root cause resolved, no regenerated docs committed).
- No new functions added and `loadCustomParamFnHook`'s branch structure is unchanged (CC unchanged), so the CRAP profile of the refactored helpers is preserved; new tests cover all three branches of the touched helper.

{"content":"# Re: dynamic `customParams[key]` breaks agentDocGenerator static analysis

```javascript
loadCustomParamFnHook(config, customParams.prSearchFnPath, 'prSearchFnPath', 'prSearchFn');
```

Both `customParams.branchNamingFnPath` and `customParams.prSearchFnPath` literal accesses are now visible to the two regexes in `js/agentDocGenerator.js:268-269`, so the keys stay in every generated agent doc (the hooks remain fully supported features — committing regenerated docs would have been wrong).
